sections.content:
Population change in Preston in 2032

The population in Preston is projected to increase from 151,869 people in 2022 to 172,921 people in 2032.

The biggest factor in this population change is net international migration, which will increase the population by 24,879 people.

This is different to the majority of areas in England, where net internal migration is projected to be the biggest factor in population change.

sections.title: Contributors to population change in Preston
sections.subtitle: How the population is projected to change, by cause
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant
sections.note: The components of change do not always sum exactly to the total population change in an area. This is primarily due to the effect of constraining the final projections to the National Population Projections for England.

sections.content:
Population change is projected by looking at births and deaths (natural change) and people moving in and out of areas. In Preston, our projections show that between 2022 and 2032:

  • More births than deaths mean that the population is projected to increase by 3,392, with 17,898 births and 14,506 deaths in Preston between 2022 and 2032. This means natural change would increase the population in Preston by 2.2%, compared with an increase of 0.2% in England.
  • Net internal migration (people moving to and from other local authorities in England) is projected to reduce the population by 7,595, with 104,657 people moving to the area and 112,252 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would decrease the population in Preston by 5.0%.
  • Net cross-border migration (between UK nations) is projected to increase the population by 427, with 4,138 people moving to the area and 3,710 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would increase the population in Preston by 0.3%.
  • Net international migration is projected to increase the population by 24,879, with 38,353 people moving to the area and 13,474 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would increase the population in Preston by 16.4%, compared with an increase of 6.5% in England.

sections.content:
Age profile in Preston in 2032

The median age in Preston is projected to rise from 36 years in 2022 to 37 years in 2032.

In England, the median age is projected to be 41 years in 2032.

In 2032, 15% of the population in Preston are projected to be aged 65 years or over, up from 14% in 2022.

sections.title: The 40 to 49 age group are set to see the largest change in Preston between 2022 and 2032
sections.subtitle: Percentages of population by 10 year age bands, 2022 and 2032
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant

sections.content:
Between 2022 and 2032, the share of the working age population (people aged 16 years to State Pension age) in Preston is projected to stay the same, at around 67%.

The old age dependency ratio (the number of people of State Pension age for every 1,000 people of working age) is projected to stay around the same, at 207 in 2032 compared with 208 in 2022.

This is below average for England in 2032 (287 per 1,000). Nationally, a high old age dependency ratio means more older people are financially reliant on the working age population to pay for pensions.

How will the number of young people change in Preston?

In 2032, 22% of people are projected to be aged 18 years and under, down from 23% in 2022.

This is above average for England in 2032 (20%).

Looking at the youngest age groups in Preston between 2022 and 2032, we can see the share of:

  • Infants (aged 0 to 4 years) will fall from 6% to 5%
  • Primary school age children (aged 5 to 11 years) will fall from 9% to 8%
  • Secondary school age children and sixth-form age (aged 12 to 18 years) will stay around the same, at 8%
